title: Apron SLAM authority, 3D road model and privacy
summary: A measured or assumed road-plane and camera project a cuboid vehicle and blank plate plane. Source-time observations are fit against multiple hypotheses; scores are not registration probabilities.
invariants: Use actual source-global integer PTS and an explicit shutter exposure separate from frame cadence.
Camera height, focal length, radial distortion, road width, lane position and vehicle dimensions are explicit hypotheses, not settled facts.
A visually estimated road edge cannot silently become an independently surveyed world-image calibration anchor.
Report geometric undersampling, model ambiguity and high residuals; abstain from plate character or registration claims when data are inadequate.
Do not retain or commit real footage, source frames, plate crops, number plates, plate text or derived identifying observations; synthetic only in Git.
Do not redistribute the user-supplied Attrill typeface without appropriate terms; third-party inference belongs behind the existing ooRexx Foreign Runtime or Macrospace boundary.
Re-use Alchemy Maths, Vision, Motion Control, Media Object Access and SLAM rather than duplicating their component authority.
procedure: Admit bounded anonymous vehicle-box samples on a monotonic source-PTS track and discard on close.
Generate a finite family of physically constrained ApronRoadScene camera/road/vehicle hypotheses.
Score box reprojection and optional estimated or surveyed road anchors independently, then rank candidates without interpreting residuals as likelihoods.
Apply explicit projected pixel sampling and shutter-motion gates to plate visibility.
Request new independent road/camera anchors if candidates are ambiguous or unanchored; retain no identifiable source data.

provenance.claim: v0.1-dev4 synthetic ooRexx geometry, ephemeral track, candidate residuals and pixel sampling gates; real ANPR unqualified
